title: Emile Christian, the Paris trombonist
summary: Briggs recalls the former Original Dixieland Jazz Band trombonist Emile Christian as a regular at the Paris Flea Pit and well liked, who vanished at the start of the war.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Well, there was another American guy named, a trombonist named Emile Christian who was in Germany at that time; is that right?
Oh, yes. Emile Christian was a --
Creole guy, New Orleans?
Yes. Emile Christian was the original trombone player of the [Original] Dixieland Jazz Band.
Right.
Yes, sure. I know him from Paris, and Emile was a regular guy, 'cause he was always with us. We were at the "Flea Pit," as I told you about.
Right.
Briggs 180
Well, Emile would always be at the "Flea Pit". He was the only guy of Billy Arnold's band, cause he was with Billy Arnold's band, that came around to see us, and stayed with us, and was with us.
Yes, Emile Christian was quite a man. He went back in 1940, I think.
I don't know whatever happened to him.
He disappeared when Germany invaded Poland. He might have passed -- went to Spain, 'cause most of the boys went to Spain, to get out, you see.
Right.
And I lost track of him, but I have a wonderful souvenir of him because he was such a wonderful man.
Right.
You see, in general, James, I believe, people who have talent are congenial. Because Emile Christian -- I mean all the boys were crazy about him.
Briggs 181
Anything he wanted, he could have. Anything.
Right.
Danny Polo, also.
